name: Ontario
title: Ontario Rebate Calculator 2026: Home Renovation Savings, Heat Pumps and More
h1: Ontario Rebate Calculator 2026: What You Could Get Back
desc: Free Ontario rebate calculator. See Home Renovation Savings rebates for heat pumps, insulation, solar, batteries and thermostats, with the official source for every amount.
intro: Answer a few questions and see which Ontario rebates fit your home, with a source for every number.
short: Ontario's Home Renovation Savings program pays $1,250 per ton (up to $7,500) for a cold-climate air-source heat pump when you heat with electricity, oil, propane or wood, and $500 per ton (up to $2,000) if you heat with Enbridge natural gas. It also pays up to $1,250 for attic insulation, up to $10,000 for solar and a battery, and $125 for a smart thermostat. The federal Greener Homes loan is closed.
faq: How much is the Ontario heat pump rebate in 2026?

Home Renovation Savings pays $1,250 per ton, up to $7,500, for a cold-climate air-source heat pump if you heat with electricity, oil, propane or wood. A ground-source heat pump pays $2,000 per ton, up to $12,000. If you heat with Enbridge natural gas the amounts are $500 per ton (up to $2,000) for air source and $3,000 for ground source.
Is there a rebate for a new gas furnace in Ontario?
No. Home Renovation Savings lists heat pumps, not furnaces, so a new gas furnace gets no rebate.
Can I get a free smart thermostat in Ontario?
The Energy Affordability Program is the free path, for households under its income limits. Everyone else can get the $125 Home Renovation Savings thermostat rebate after buying one.
Is the federal Greener Homes loan still open?
No. The last day to apply was October 1, 2025. People who were already approved can continue.

programs.name: Home Renovation Savings: air-source heat pump
programs.rules: Cold-climate model. You heat with electricity, oil, propane or wood. No home energy assessment needed. Not a new build lived in for 6 months or less.

programs.name: Home Renovation Savings: ground-source heat pump
programs.rules: The only way to reach $12,000. You heat with electricity, oil, propane or wood.

programs.name: Home Renovation Savings: air-source heat pump (Enbridge gas home)
programs.rules: You need an active Enbridge Gas residential account and heat mainly with a gas furnace or boiler. Rentals get the same lower amounts whatever the fuel.

programs.name: Home Renovation Savings: ground-source heat pump (Enbridge gas home)
programs.rules: You need an active Enbridge Gas residential account and heat mainly with a gas furnace or boiler.

programs.name: Home Renovation Savings: heat pump water heater
programs.rules: Part of the assessment track: a home energy assessment before and after the work.

programs.name: Home Renovation Savings: attic insulation, no assessment
programs.rules: Up to $1,250 without a home energy assessment. The official page also shows lower steps by starting R-value.

programs.name: Home Renovation Savings: attic insulation with assessment
programs.rules: Needs a home energy assessment before and after. Pays $1,500, $1,200 or $900 depending on your starting R-value.

programs.name: Home Renovation Savings: whole-home insulation with assessment
programs.rules: Needs a home energy assessment before and after. Total insulation rebates are capped at $7,700. Walls, basement, crawlspace and more are paid by area.

programs.name: Home Renovation Savings: solar
programs.rules: $1,000 per kW, up to $5,000 and 50% of cost. You cannot also take a net-metering agreement with your utility.

programs.name: Home Renovation Savings: battery
programs.rules: $300 per kWh, up to $5,000 and 50% of cost. Only with new solar. Solar and battery together are capped at $10,000.

programs.name: Home Renovation Savings: smart thermostat
programs.rules: Enbridge gas-heated home, or electrically heated or cooled home. Listed models only. Upload the receipt within 60 days. One thermostat rebate per home.

programs.name: Save on Energy Peak Perks
programs.rules: $75 on enrolling, then $20 a year. Needs central AC or a heat pump run by an eligible Wi-Fi thermostat. Not for high-rise units.

programs.name: Home Renovation Savings: appliances
programs.rules: Heat pump dryer $200, induction cooktop or range $150, washer $75, fridge $50, freezer $50, dishwasher $25. Replace an existing electric appliance. Apply within 60 days.

programs.name: Energy Affordability Program (free upgrades)
programs.rules: Free upgrades for households under the income limits, from $48,220 for 1 person to $96,439 for 4 people, or on OW, ODSP or OESP. Call 1-844-770-3148.

programs.name: Toronto Home Energy Loan Program
programs.rules: A city loan repaid on your property tax bill, up to 10% of your home's assessed value, for up to 20 years. Confirm the current rate with the City.

programs.name: Better Homes Ottawa loan
programs.rules: Repaid on your property tax bill, up to 10% of your home's assessed value, 20 years. 0% for households under the income limits. Not for gas upgrades.

programs.name: RetrofitWR loan (GrandBridge customers)
programs.rules: 2.5% fixed for 10 or 15 years, repaid on your GrandBridge Energy bill. Only for GrandBridge customers in Cambridge and North Dumfries. A free Energy Coach is open to homeowners across Waterloo Region.

programs.name: National Heat Pump Rebate (federal, not open yet)
programs.rules: Announced October 8, 2026 and expected to launch in early 2027. $10,000 is for households below the median income and $2,000 for other eligible homeowners. The income line and eligible homes are not published, so this is shown but not added to your total.

notes: A new gas furnace gets no Home Renovation Savings rebate.
Amounts are the most a program pays. Your rebate depends on the equipment, the work and your final invoice.
